newsitem.title: USA: U.S. S&P 500 futures close sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. S&P 500 futures close sharply higher.

text.p: U.S. Standard & Poor's 500s closed sharply higher in a late rally that fed on technical factors, rather than any fresh fundamental factors, traders and analysts said.

While a rise in the Redbook retail sales index and the re-election of Representative Newt Gingrich as Speaker of the House were cited as positives for the market, most traders said the S&P futures market was driven higher by technicals.
They said selling pressure dried up, giving locals and several large retail houses the chance to bid the market the higher, they said.
The surge of buying touched off buy-stop orders throughout the afternoon and was largely responsible for March's advance to 760.20, above Monday's high of 759.80.

Traders said the heaviest buy-stop orders were hit between 752.50 and 754.00. They also said one European-based firm was actively trading arbitrage buy programs at about a premium of 6.50 points to the cash index.

March S&Ps closed slightly above fair value, which is at a premium of 5.08 points to cash. Arbitrage sell programs were reported earlier in the day when March's premium to cash narrowed to 4.50 points.
While S&Ps powered higher, the Dow Jones Industrial Average ended at a record high close for the second day in a row.
One stock market analyst attributed the Dow's performance to the attractiveness of economically sensitive stocks, which largely make up the Dow Industrials.

Nikkei 225 contracts remained sharply lower throughout the day, with March closing down 570 points at 18,935. March set a contract low of 18,875, bombarded by follow-through selling for most of the day, traders said.

At the end of pit trade, March S&Ps were 8.95 points higher at 759.65, KCBT Value Lines were up 5.15 at 694.15, New Composites rose 3.85 at 400.05, Midcap 400s were 2.00 higher at 261.10 and Nasdaq 100s jumped 14.10 to 874.10.
